inputs.xtext_rule_text:
TransitionSuccession returns SysML::SuccessionAsUsage :
	ownedRelationship += EmptySourceEndMember 
	ownedRelationship += ConnectorEndMember
;

notes: No corpus instance was offered in the pack, because the production contributes no keyword of its own to match on. The cited line is an instance nonetheless: it is the target of a 'then', which is where the clause puts a TransitionSuccession.
decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.18.3. The only difference from the Xtext is the name of the first member: the clause writes EmptyEndMember (`ownedRelatedElement += EmptyFeature`, and EmptyFeature is `{}`), the Xtext writes EmptySourceEndMember. Both derive empty, so the two accept the same language and this is a naming difference rather than a disagreement. The clause's name is taken, because EmptyEndMember is a production of the specification with its own unit and EmptySourceEndMember appears in no clause. A transition succession therefore contributes exactly the tokens of its ConnectorEndMember: the source end is implicit, supplied by the transition that owns it.

evidence.note: States the production; the rule is its transcription.

Line 61 `then Wait;` — the TransitionSuccession is the `Wait` after 'then', which is its ConnectorEndMember. The empty end contributes no tokens, which is why the succession reads as a bare target name.
Second opinion. Same rule under a different name for the empty end.
